messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the development of a mane in adult males. The gene responsible for mane growth (often referred to as the *M* allele) is dominant over the allele that results in a lack of mane (*m*). Thus, when a male lion inherits at least one copy of the *M* allele from either parent, it will develop a full mane. This trait is not only visually striking but also plays a role in sexual selection and territorial displays.
